get.description:
Cursor-paginated feed of Midnight economic activity events.

**Scope.** Includes `take`, `add_collateral`, `remove_collateral`, `repay`, `withdraw`, `liquidation`, and `market_created`. Admin/auth/fee/flashloan/internal accounting events are excluded from v1.

**Account filter.** `account` matches the affected position account: maker/taker for `take`, `on_behalf` for repay/withdraw/collateral events, and borrower for liquidations. `market_created` rows are excluded when `account` is provided.

**Pagination.** Response follows the list envelope: `{ cursor, data }`. Pass back `cursor` verbatim on the next call. A `null` cursor means the last page. Ordering is fixed to block timestamp with deterministic block/log tie-breakers.

**Cache.** `public, max-age=2, stale-while-revalidate=1`.

get.description:
Cursor-paginated list of a user's current **post-take** Midnight positions.

**Position type.** `type` is `lend` for lenders (`credit > 0`), `borrow` for borrowers (`debt > 0`), or `collateral_only` for users who have fully repaid/withdrawn but still have residual collateral parked under the market (`credit == 0 && debt == 0` with non-empty `collaterals`). `units` is the derived maturity-value projection: credit for lenders, debt for borrowers, `0` for `collateral_only`. Positions with no credit, no debt, and no remaining collateral are **closed** and excluded.

**Computed fields.** `cost_basis` (average cost method, WAD-scaled, in loan-asset units) and `effective_rate_wad` (IRR+ — the single annualized rate that reproduces the current face value from each remaining buy's capital) are `null` until the indexer has enough user history to attribute.

**Lots.** Each item includes a `lots[]` array — the chronological per-entry breakdown reconstructed from chain history (`remaining_pv`, `remaining_fv`, `remaining_fv_wad`, `entry_timestamp`). Sufficient to reconstruct every Make/Take/Withdraw/Repay/Liquidate that touched the position and to project value forward under a hypothetical Make/Take.

**Filters.** `chain_ids` is required when `loan_assets` is provided. Range filters exist on `units`, `credit`, `debt`, `cost_basis`, `effective_rate_wad`, and `last_activity_block_timestamp`. `active_only=true` excludes matured markets.

**Pagination.** Response envelope: `{ cursor, data }`.

**Cache.** `public, max-age=2, stale-while-revalidate=1`.

**Filters.** All optional. `addresses` requires `chain_ids` to disambiguate. `markets` is capped at 100. With no filters, every distinct token across every chain is returned (cardinality is bounded by deduplication).

**Response shape.** Batch envelope: `{ data: [...] }`. No pagination — token cardinality is naturally small.

**Cache.** `public, max-age=30, stale-while-revalidate=60`.

get.description:
Returns the distinct oracles used as collateral price feeds by Midnight markets matching the filters, paired with the latest raw quote from `realtime.oracle_realtime` and trust-signal enrichments.

**Filters.** All optional. `addresses` requires `chain_ids` to disambiguate. `markets` is capped at 100. With no filters, every distinct oracle across every chain is returned.

**Response shape.** Batch envelope: `{ data: [...] }`. `price.value` is the raw oracle quote as a bigint string — no USD conversion is applied.

**Enrichments.** The endpoint `filters` decide *which* oracles are returned. Per-oracle enrichments are **oracle-global** trust signals — they are not narrowed by the same filters. Each item carries:
- `collateral_assets` / `loan_assets` — distinct asset pairs across **all** Morpho V1 markets and Midnight markets using this oracle.
- `total_value_secured_usd` — sum of `supplyAssetsUsd + collateralAssetsUsd` across **all** Morpho V1 markets using this oracle. Null when any contributing market is missing a USD price.
- `trusted_by` — curators of Morpho V1 vaults that allocate to markets using this oracle, sorted by curator id.

**Cache.** `public, max-age=30, stale-while-revalidate=60`.

get.description:
Returns the list of Midnight-supported chains, each with its lowercased chain name, the latest block (number and hash) the indexer has committed to its database, and a server-computed status comparing indexed Midnight activity with processed activity. Use `latest_indexed_block` to detect when the API is far behind the chain tip and `activity_sync_status` to detect whether indexed activity has been processed.

**Response shape.** Batch envelope: `{ data: [...] }`. Each entry contains `chain_id`, `name`, `latest_indexed_block` (an object with `number` — a bigint serialized as a string — and `hash`), and `activity_sync_status`. Chains whose indexer state is not yet provisioned are omitted.

**Activity sync statuses.** `healthy` means processing has caught up with indexed activity. `pending` means indexed activity exists but has not been processed yet. `behind` means processing is behind indexed activity. `no_activity` means no indexed activity marker exists for the pipeline.

**Cache.** `public, max-age=2, stale-while-revalidate=5`.

get.description: Returns a bundle-ready quote for the requested assets or units, plus expected best/worst average prices and maximum executable liquidity. The endpoint optimizes for successful target-aware bundle execution under contention: `takes` are best-priced per-offer caps and their total can exceed the requested target, giving a bundle executor fallback liquidity when earlier offers are partially consumed or skipped. Use the returned takes with a bundle abstraction that stops at your requested target and applies your max/min asset or unit protections. If you execute the takes independently with Midnight.take, do not submit every returned unit blindly: clamp each take to your remaining target and current takeability, or you may execute more than intended. If the requested size cannot be fully satisfied at quote time under the selected guard, the endpoint returns 422.

422.description: Requested quote size cannot be fully satisfied.

parameters.name: average_worst_price
parameters.description: Optional average weighted-price guard for the requested target. `asks` must execute at or below this value; `bids` must execute at or above it. The guard applies to the expected target fill, not to the sum of all returned take caps. Mutually exclusive with `slippage`.

parameters.name: slippage
parameters.description: Optional slippage percentage used to derive `average_worst_price` from the quoted `average_best_price` for the requested target. Slippage constrains the expected target fill, not the sum of all returned take caps. For `asks`, the guard increases by slippage; for `bids`, it decreases by slippage. Range: 0.1 to 100, with at most one decimal place. Mutually exclusive with `average_worst_price`.

parameters.name: units
parameters.description: Target unit amount. Provide exactly one of `assets` or `units`.

parameters.name: assets
parameters.description: Target assets amount. Provide exactly one of `assets` or `units`.

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: Book side to quote (`asks` or `bids`).

parameters.name: market-id
parameters.description: Market ID whose book to quote (`market_id` in responses).

info.title: Midnight API
info.description:
> [!warning]
> The Midnight API is in alpha. Expect frequent breaking changes and unstable behavior.

REST API for Morpho Midnight, the fixed-rate lending protocol.

tags.name: Activity
tags.description:
A **Midnight activity** item is one indexed economic protocol event. One onchain transaction can emit multiple activity rows.

### Event types

`take`, `add_collateral`, `remove_collateral`, `repay`, `withdraw`, `liquidation`, and `market_created`.

Admin, authorization, fee, flashloan, and internal accounting events are intentionally excluded from v1.

### Account filter

`account` matches the affected position account, not only the transaction caller: maker/taker for takes, `on_behalf` for repay/withdraw/collateral events, and borrower for liquidations. `market_created` rows are excluded when `account` is set.

### Sorting

Ordering is fixed to block timestamp with deterministic block/log tie-breakers. Use `sort_direction` to switch between newest-first and oldest-first.

tags.name: Markets
tags.description:
A **Midnight market** is a fixed-rate market parameterized by a loan token, a sorted list of collaterals (each with LLTV, max LIF, and oracle), a maturity timestamp, and a recovery close factor (RCF) threshold. The market id is derived from the market struct + chain id + contract address and is **globally unique** — the bare id alone is sufficient to address a market.

### Filters

Chain-scoped address filters (`loan_assets`, `collateral_assets`, `oracle_addresses`, `enter_gates`, `liquidator_gates`) require `chain_ids` to disambiguate — e.g. searching `loan_assets=0xA0b8…` without `chain_ids` is rejected with a 400. Time filters (`maturity_gte`, `maturity_lte`) accept unix seconds; `active_only=true` is a shortcut for `maturity > now`.

### Sortable fields

`total_units` (default), `withdrawable`, `maturity`, `rcf_threshold`, `creation_block_timestamp`.

tags.name: Positions
tags.description:
A **Midnight position** is a user's current post-take state on a given market: credit & debt, pending fee, loss factor, per-collateral balances, and — when computable from history — `cost_basis` and `effective_rate_wad`.

### Lender vs borrower

A position's `type` is `lend` when `credit > 0` (the user is holding shares), or `borrow` when `debt > 0`. `units` is the derived maturity-value projection: credit for lenders, debt for borrowers. A position with `credit == 0 && debt == 0` is considered **closed** — the detail endpoint returns 404.

### Cost basis & effective rate

- `cost_basis` uses the **average cost method**: entries add to the basis, exits reduce it proportionally. WAD-scaled bigint in loan-asset units; `null` when the position has no history attributable to the user (e.g. received via transfer).
- `effective_rate_wad` is **IRR+** — the single annualized rate that compounds each remaining buy's capital from entry time to maturity to produce the current face value. WAD-scaled; `null` until sufficient history is available.

### Lots

Each open position carries a `lots[]` array, ordered by `entry_timestamp`. Each lot is one entry (Make/Take buy) and tracks:

- `remaining_pv` — capital still attributable to this lot, in loan-asset units.
- `remaining_fv` — face value still attributable to this lot, in loan-asset units.
- `remaining_fv_wad` — face value still attributable, WAD-scaled (used to compute the effective rate).
- `entry_timestamp` — when the entry was made, in unix seconds.

Lots are **not an onchain concept**: they are reconstructed by the indexer by replaying the full position history (`Take`, `Withdraw`, `Repay`, `Liquidate`, …). Exits scale each lot's remainders proportionally (average-cost method). The list is therefore sufficient to **reconstruct every Make/Take/Withdraw/Repay/Liquidate that touched the position** — both Make/Take extrapolation forward and complete past-activity attribution fall out of it. Closed positions (`credit == 0 && debt == 0`) are excluded from this endpoint and therefore expose no lots.

### Filters

`chain_ids` is required when `loan_assets` is provided. Range filters exist on `units`, `credit`, `debt`, `cost_basis`, `effective_rate_wad`, and `last_activity_block_timestamp`.

### Sortable fields

`last_activity_block_timestamp` (default), `units`, `credit`, `debt`, `maturity`, `cost_basis`, `effective_rate_wad`.

tags.name: Groups
tags.description:
Active onchain mempool offer groups for a user.

### Response

List envelope: `{ cursor, data: [...] }`. Each item contains the group id, chain id, representative active offer limits, and the latest indexed consumed amount. Takeability, raw offers, market ids, offer hashes, and Merkle proof metadata are intentionally excluded.

tags.name: Tokens
tags.description:
Distinct tokens used as **loan asset** or **collateral** by Midnight markets matching the filters, enriched with ERC-20 metadata and the latest USD price from `realtime.asset_realtime`.

### Universe

The universe of returned tokens is always **derived from markets** — this endpoint never invents addresses; it only enriches addresses that appear on at least one market matching `chain_ids` and/or `markets`. Pass `addresses` to further intersect with a known address set (requires `chain_ids`).

### Response

Batch envelope: `{ data: [...] }`. No pagination — token cardinality is naturally small. `markets` is capped at 100 per call.

tags.name: Oracles
tags.description:
Distinct oracles used as collateral price feeds by Midnight markets matching the filters, paired with the latest raw onchain quote from `realtime.oracle_realtime`.

### Universe

The universe of returned oracles is always **derived from markets** — only oracles referenced by at least one collateral on at least one market matching the filters are returned.

### Response

Batch envelope: `{ data: [...] }`. `price.value` is the raw oracle quote as a bigint string — no USD conversion is applied. `markets` is capped at 100 per call.

tags.name: Offers
tags.description:
Raw onchain mempool offers indexed from the Midnight mempool contract.

### Response

List envelope: `{ cursor, data: [...] }`. Each item contains only decoded offer struct fields. Derived Router group state, takeability, hashes, market ids, and Merkle proof metadata are intentionally excluded.

tags.name: Chains
tags.description:
Midnight-supported chains, each with the latest block committed by the indexer and an activity processing status.

### Use case

The Midnight app polls this endpoint to detect when the API is lagging behind the chain tip and whether indexed Midnight activity has been processed. When the gap exceeds the app's freshness budget, it falls back to reading the on-chain state directly instead of serving stale indexed data. The endpoint is **not** a global health check — see `/health` for that.

### Activity sync statuses

- `healthy` — processing has caught up with indexed activity.
- `pending` — indexed activity exists but has not been processed yet.
- `behind` — processing is behind indexed activity.
- `no_activity` — indexer has not recorded activity for that chain and pipeline yet.

### Response

Batch envelope: `{ data: [...] }`. Each entry contains `chain_id`, lowercased `name`, `latest_indexed_block` (an object with `number` — a bigint serialized as a string — and `hash`), and `activity_sync_status`. Statuses are server-computed from indexed and processed Midnight activity; raw marker blocks are intentionally not exposed. Chains whose indexer state is not yet provisioned are omitted from the response.

available_assets.description: Maximum assets available from the returned take caps if they remain executable. This can exceed the requested target so bundle execution has fallback liquidity.

available_units.description: Maximum units available from the returned take caps if they remain executable. This can exceed the requested target so bundle execution has fallback liquidity.

takes.description: Best-priced signed take caps intended for target-aware bundle execution. Each `units` value is the maximum that offer may contribute, not an exact allocation for the requested target; the sum can exceed the requested size so a bundle executor can skip stale offers and still fill the target. If you call Midnight.take directly instead of using target-aware bundle execution, clamp each take to your remaining target and current takeability, otherwise you may execute more than intended.
